entry.title: Customise XigmaNas build, adding drivers and Navidrome
entry.content:
Let's build XigmaNas from source!

What could go wrong?

I am a total FreeBSD noob and a terrible <s>C/Python</s> programmer. But I love me some XigmaNas. I really like the "firmware" model, it bootstraps itself up into a RAM disk and the original boot files and OS are never accessible, so in theory can't get corrupted. I've been running it at home for years, I forget how many, maybe 10 years? And it is rock solid.

XigmaNAS is an Open Source Storage NAS (Network-Attached Storage) distribution based on FreeBSD.

Navidrome is a self-hosted, open source music server and streamer.

What are you doing!?

Building an OS from source can be a little daunting.

Which release of XigmaNas are you trying to build? Why are you doing this?

Maybe you don't need to do this at all? Maybe bhyve or a vm can do it for you?

For stability reasons I suggest to NOT use the Xigmanas trunk, but the last stable release. Just based on the vibes. And my pain.

Today (Oct 2026) that is 14.3.0.5

But hey, go for it.

You need to get your ducks in a row.

The Xigma release will reference a FreeBSD release, e.g. for XigmaNas-14.3 this is FreeBSD releng/14.3

You need the ports branch to match the FreeBSD branch.

releng - "release engineering branch", a little FreeBSDism.

This guide is to help me bake in the realtek-re-kmod drivers for the RTL8125 chipset, used in my cheap TPLink 2.5Gbe card.

And to add Navidrome as a service.

The XigmaNas releases are not exactly reproducible builds. If you are expert at FreeBSD, ports and make then you will probably have a better time than I did.

The more I learn the more I see that this is not a XigmaNas issue, but more a FreeBSD issue.

The main issue is building the ports. Due to many dependencies, transitive dependencies, missing libraries, changes between versions of FreeBSD we find DEPENDENCY HELL. Ooooo. Go search for "freebsd cython conflict". It seems FreeBSD has been a bit laissez faire in dependency management between, or even within, versions...

Orientation

I am operating on this repository - https://svn.code.sf.net/p/xigmanas/code/branches/14.3.0.5/

In the /build folder we find the main make.sh which delegates pretty much everything to functions.inc.

Within functions.inc I found it helpful to find the menu item in the build I was having trouble with and follow the code from there, usually through a choice.

The /ports directory is important. Here we find all the Makefiles for each port, and also a /distfiles folder that has some "special" dependencies. Notice also the /ports/Makefile here.

The /kernel-config folder holds a modules.files file, which shows the kernel drivers being used.

Branches, tags, ports and kernel

It took many attempts to find this. This is NOT the right branch for the ports, but I'm pretty sure there is no right branch. This branch produced the least errors.

Important - much pain if the branches don't line up

FreeBSD: releng/14.3 (https://git.freebsd.org/src.git) (Commit: 833d39bd2e38421a14ea489a956261a0fa993fbc)

Xigmanas: 14.3.0.5 (https://svn.code.sf.net/p/xigmanas/code/branches/14.3.0.5/) (Revision: 10655)

Ports: 14.2-eol (https://cgit.freebsd.org/ports/tree/databases?h=14.2-eol)
(Commit: 4e450f33b9f9cf668688f9c439c58871751e2bbb)

git -C /usr/ports rev-parse HEAD 4e450f33b9f9cf668688f9c439c58871751e2bbb root@xigma-build:/usr/local/xigmanas # git -C /usr/src rev-parse HEAD 833d39bd2e38421a14ea489a956261a0fa993fbc root@xigma-build:/usr/local/xigmanas # svn info /usr/local/xigmanas/svn | grep Revision Revision: 10655

Fix the ports

With 14.2-eol I had three failures, which can be resolved:

php84-APCu

/usr/local/xigmanas/svn/build/ports/php84-APCu/Makefile

Can be fixed by updating the Makefile to be like the one from trunk - remove lang/php84 dependency.

BUILD_DEPENDS=	${NONEXISTENT}:devel/pecl-APCu \
		php84:lang/php84

Replace with: BUILD_DEPENDS= ${NONEXISTENT}:devel/pecl-APCu

samba422

Note: we do this before make.sh is run.

samba422 - cython conflict - removing cython3 fixed it.

I cannot figure out what causes this.

Removing cython3 removes the conflict.

pkg-static delete -f py311-cython3

We will need to run this before we run make.sh

vbox

vbox seems to be hitting swap issues!

The error message suggests to add to Makefile /usr/ports/emulators/virtualbox-ose-72/Makefile in /usr/ports - MAKE_JOBS_UNSAFE=yes which limits make to single thread. :(

We can set in make.conf instead and scope it to the "problem areas". Yes, Claude told me this.

.if ${.CURDIR:M*/devel/llvm19}
MAKE_JOBS_NUMBER=4
.endif

python311

Probably related to cython? Who knows.

The shipped Makefile for the XigmaNas version of python311 expects the /usr/ports/ version of python311 to have been built.

This error turns up while installing ports, so very late in the game.

cd /usr/ports/lang/python311
make stage

This seems very odd, the XIgamNas version seems to just want to install the host python311?

I do not understand what I am looking at.

This line in the Makefile seems... wrong?

DEP_STAGEDIR= ${PORTSDIR}/lang/python311/work/stage

Realtek driver

The realtek card I care about uses chipset RTL8125. The realtek drivers (re) shipped by FreeBSD DO NOT support this at this time. Or in v15 either.

Hence we build the ports/net/realtek-re-kmod port and install.

Create QEMU FreeBSD

https://download.freebsd.org/ftp/releases/amd64/amd64/ISO-IMAGES/14.3/

Use the FreeBSD-14.3-RELEASE-amd64-disc1.iso.

Time has moved on and 14.3 is no longer hosted there (14.4+ as of right now). You may need to shop around.

Make the FreeBSD build VM

Create a FreeBSD 14.3 build machine. I have allocated 16GB RAM and 140GB drive space. You might get away with less RAM. The build takes hours, so give it what you can. I did find I ran out of diskspace at 100GB... so 140GB is good.

#!/bin/bash

# this a build machine, need CPU
# 140GB HDD, 16GB RAM and 8 cores 
qemu-img create -f qcow2 freebsd-img.qcow2 140G

# ssh port 22 is forwarded to 2222
qemu-system-x86_64 -cdrom ../FreeBSD-14.3-RELEASE-amd64-disc1.iso -cpu host -enable-kvm -m 16384 -smp 8 -drive file=./freebsd-img.qcow2,format=qcow2 -net nic -net user,hostfwd=tcp::2222-:22

Had to install qemu-system-x86_64 on my host, but all good.

Installing FreeBSD

Pretty much just accept all defaults.

Install with lib32, NOTE: not the lib32-dbg

No point installing ports or src as these are pulled later via git.

Used Auto UFS/GPT and the whole disk. The XigmaNas dev guide suggests two partitions, a 4GB swap and a larger /. I just took the defaults, which was a 4GB swap.

Enter new root password. It rhymes with groot.

Accept all defaults for ipv4 and ipv6.

Set timezone and region.

Do not add any users we will run as root.

And reboot.

Prepare the VM - enable ssh

Enable SSH on the VM:

# run this on the VM
pkg install -y nano git subversion

# uncomment this in /etc/ssh/ssh_config
# PasswordAuthentication yes
nano /etc/ssh/ssh_config

# enable this in /etc/ssh/sshd_config
# PermitRootLogin yes
nano /etc/ssh/sshd_config

service sshd restart

mkdir /usr/local/xigmanas

# used later for sshfs
mkdir ~/xigma

SSH to the VM

Can get the ip address locally via ifconfig and look for the virtbr virtual bridge, this time it's 192.168.122.1.

ssh root@192.168.122.1 -p2222

You may need to remove the old key if this is not your first attempt. Read the error message.

Add ssh-fs fileshare

You can do this later if you want. Assuming this build actually works we want to be able to copy the disk image back to our desktop.

On the VM I made this directory in my (root) home ~/xigma. And you should already have this directory /usr/local/xigmanas in the VM.

sshfs -o port=2222 root@192.168.122.1:/usr/local/xigmanas ~/xigma

The XigmaNas Readme - hmmmm...

Follow the readme at https://sourceforge.net/p/xigmanas/code/HEAD/tree/branches/14.3.0.5/build/README but it's misleading.

It's pretty much correct, just any mention of ports, or pulling the ports has to be taken with a large chunk of salt.

Primarily it does not specify where the ports come from, which leads to much cursing.

We pull the BSD source and ports ourselves.

Prepare the build environment

Update /etc/make.conf

Read the file in the source for the latest.

OPTIONS_UNSET=X11
DEFAULT_VERSIONS+=mysql=8.0
DEFAULT_VERSIONS+=ssl=base
DEFAULT_VERSIONS+=php=8.4

# due to 14.3 being so "old", i mean it's been over a year...
ALLOW_UNSUPPORTED_SYSTEM=yes
# oh my
DISABLE_VULNERABILITIES=yes

# vbox build blows up the swap
.if ${.CURDIR:M*/devel/llvm19}
MAKE_JOBS_NUMBER=4
.endif

Get the "right" ports

Now get the ports up to date with dependancies.

# update the ports tree
rm -rf /usr/ports
git clone --depth 1 --branch 14.2-eol https://git.FreeBSD.org/ports.git /usr/ports

# pull the src - note: releng/14.3 - or do this later via the build menu
# although with --depth 1 this way is faster ~350MB vs ~1.8GB
rm -rf /usr/src
git clone --depth 1 -b releng/14.3 https://git.freebsd.org/src.git /usr/src

# Pull the source for XigmaNas 14.3.0.5
cd /usr/local/xigmanas && svn co https://svn.code.sf.net/p/xigmanas/code/branches/14.3.0.5/ svn

We want all packages built from the same sources to avoid any weird dependancy issues. Ha!

Edit the php84-APCu Makefile

/usr/local/xigmanas/svn/build/ports/php84-APCu/Makefile

Can be fixed by updating the Makefile to be like the one from trunk - remove lang/php84 dependency.

BUILD_DEPENDS=	${NONEXISTENT}:devel/pecl-APCu \
		php84:lang/php84

Replace with: BUILD_DEPENDS= ${NONEXISTENT}:devel/pecl-APCu

Adding the navidrome port

While we still have nano available, and before running the make.sh.

cp -R /usr/ports/multimedia/navidrome/ /usr/local/xigmanas/svn/build/ports/navidrome
echo "ON" > /usr/local/xigmanas/svn/build/ports/navidrome/pkg-state

Update the /usr/local/xigmanas/svn/build/ports/Makefile and add:

    SUBDIR += navidrome

Update the Navidrome /usr/local/xigmanas/svn/build/ports/navidrome/Makefile

Add:

# add this near the top somewhere, or we get a lot interactive prompts
BATCH=yes

# add this after the post-install: target
post-stage:
	@${MKDIR} ${XIGMANAS_ROOTFS}${PREFIX}/bin ${XIGMANAS_ROOTFS}${PREFIX}/etc/rc.d ${XIGMANAS_ROOTFS}${PREFIX}/etc/navidrome
	@${INSTALL_PROGRAM} -v ${STAGEDIR}${PREFIX}/bin/navidrome ${XIGMANAS_ROOTFS}${PREFIX}/bin
	@${INSTALL_SCRIPT} -v ${STAGEDIR}${PREFIX}/etc/rc.d/navidrome ${XIGMANAS_ROOTFS}${PREFIX}/etc/rc.d
	@${INSTALL_DATA} -v ${STAGEDIR}${PREFIX}/etc/navidrome/config.toml.sample ${XIGMANAS_ROOTFS}${PREFIX}/etc/navidrome

Adding the realtek port

We will build the port, but later we will NOT install it. The install goes to the modules folder instead of ports.

cp -R /usr/ports/net/realtek-re-kmod/ /usr/local/xigmanas/svn/build/ports/realtek-re-kmod
echo "ON" > /usr/local/xigmanas/svn/build/ports/realtek-re-kmod/pkg-state

Update the /usr/local/xigmanas/svn/build/ports/Makefile and add:

    SUBDIR += realtek-re-kmod

Making the memory disk bigger

After including Navidrome the image exceeds the size of the memory disk. We need to extend that for the creation of the LiveCD ISO and for the actual memory disk when xigmanas is running.

The two files (rc and functions.inc) MUST agree on the memory disk size - in this case 1600MB

Edit the /usr/local/xigmanas/svn/etc/rc file:

Replace:

# Fixed values requested by build/make.sh
MDLOCALSIZE=1332m
SWAPSIZE=512m

With:

# Fixed values requested by build/make.sh
MDLOCALSIZE=1600m
SWAPSIZE=512m

Edit the /usr/local/xigmanas/svn/build/functions.inc file.

Note the XIGMANAS_MDLOCAL_SIZE variable.

Replace:

#	Size in MB of the MFS Root filesystem that will include all FreeBSD binary
#	and XigmaNAS® WebGUI/Scripts. Keep this file very small! This file is unzipped
#	to a RAM disk at XigmaNAS® startup.
#	The image must fit on 2GB CF/USB.
#	Actual size of MDLOCAL is defined in /etc/rc line 38.
XIGMANAS_MFSROOT_SIZE=132
XIGMANAS_MDLOCAL_SIZE=1192
XIGMANAS_MDLOCAL_MINI_SIZE=36
#	Now image size is less than 500MB (up to 476MiB - alignment)
XIGMANAS_IMG_SIZE=460
if [ "amd64" = ${XIGMANAS_ARCH} ]; then
	XIGMANAS_MFSROOT_SIZE=144
	XIGMANAS_MDLOCAL_SIZE=1332
	XIGMANAS_MDLOCAL_MINI_SIZE=52
	XIGMANAS_IMG_SIZE=500
fi

With:

#       Size in MB of the MFS Root filesystem that will include all FreeBSD binary
#       and XigmaNAS® WebGUI/Scripts. Keep this file very small! This file is unzipped
#       to a RAM disk at XigmaNAS® startup.
#       The image must fit on 2GB CF/USB.
#       Actual size of MDLOCAL is defined in /etc/rc line 38.
XIGMANAS_MFSROOT_SIZE=132
XIGMANAS_MDLOCAL_SIZE=1600
XIGMANAS_MDLOCAL_MINI_SIZE=36
#       Now image size is less than 500MB (up to 476MiB - alignment)
XIGMANAS_IMG_SIZE=460
if [ "amd64" = ${XIGMANAS_ARCH} ]; then
        XIGMANAS_MFSROOT_SIZE=144
        XIGMANAS_MDLOCAL_SIZE=1600
        XIGMANAS_MDLOCAL_MINI_SIZE=52
        XIGMANAS_IMG_SIZE=500
fi

Build some prerequisites

# removes the pkg we installed - git, subversion, nano and a few other things
pkg delete -y -f \*
cd /usr/ports/shells/bash && make BATCH=yes install clean

cd /usr/ports/ports-mgmt/portupgrade && make BATCH=yes install clean

cd /usr/ports/sysutils/cdrtools && make BATCH=yes install clean

cd /usr/ports/devel/subversion && make BATCH=yes install clean

cd /usr/ports/devel/git && make BATCH=yes install clean

# to fix problem with installing ports
cd /usr/ports/lang/python311 && make BATCH=yes stage

Build XigmaNas - run the make file

Remove the cython problem and run make.sh.

pkg-static delete -y -f py311-cython3

/usr/local/xigmanas/svn/build/make.sh

And it begins...

-------------------------------------------------------------
		Build Environment XigmaNAS® 
-------------------------------------------------------------
Choice Menu:

1) - Update XIGMANAS_SVNDIR to latest XigmaNAS Source Files.
2) - Enter Compile Menu.

-------------------------------------------------------------
Generate Images:
10) - Create 'Embedded.img.xz' File.         (Firmware Update)
11) - Create 'LiveUSB.img.gz MBR' File.   (Rawrite to USB Key)
12) - Create 'LiveUSB.img.gz GPT' File.   (Rawrite to USB Key)
13) - Create 'LiveCD' (ISO) File.
14) - Create 'LiveCD-Tin' (ISO) Without 'Embedded' File.
15) - Create 'Full' (TGZ) Update File.
16) - Create All Release images at once.
-------------------------------------------------------------
17) - Create translations xigmanas.pot file from Source files.

*)  - Exit.

1 - We can skip. it just pulls the "https://svn.code.sf.net/p/xigmanas/code/trunk" again. Useful if you maintained this build machine.

2 - We MUST run this. Must.

2 - Compile Menu

-------------------------------------------------------------
		Build Environment XigmaNAS®                  
-------------------------------------------------------------
Compile Menu:

1) - Update FreeBSD Source Tree and Ports Collections.
2) - Create Filesystem Structure.
3) - Build/Install the Kernel.
4) - Build World.
5) - Import base-ports to their locations.
6) - Build Ports.
7) - Build Bootloader.
8) - Add Necessary Libraries.
9) - Modify File Permissions.
-------------------------------------------------------------

*) - Exit Compile Menu.

2.1 Update FreeBSD Source Tree and Ports Collections.

    1. Pull FreeBSD src source tree - this is a clone, deletes the /usr/src directory and clones
    1. Update FreeBSD src source tree - is a pull
    1. Fetch and install binary updates - updates this vm install
    1. Update ports collection - does a git pull on the /usr/ports
    1. Upgrade pkg on host - like an apt update/upgrade on this vm

If you already pulled the FreeBSD source then you can skip this whole menu item.

If not - Run 1. That is all.

2.2 - Create Filesystem Structure.

Yes - run this. Sets things up in /usr/local/xigmanas/rootfs

2.3 - Build/Install the Kernel.

  1. Apply kernel patches
  2. Build kernel
  3. Install kernel + modules

Run all of these. You can select all three at once.

The install kernel + modules step is the bit we need to copy later to install the realtek driver.

2.4 - Build World.

Yes - run this. Copies a bunch files around.

2.5 - Import base-ports to their locations.

Yes - run this. Updates some of the /usr/ports/distfiles with build specific things.

2.6 - Build Ports.

    1. Build ports
    1. Build ports (dev only, no preselection)
    1. Re-build ports (dev only)
    1. Install ports

Run 1 & 4.

When we run 4 deselect the realtek-re-mod port.

Rerunning the "Install" step is very brittle. You MUST rebuild or make clean the port before trying to reinstall.

This takes ages. Like, 8 hours. And sometimes has a dialog you have to hit enter on. Although that might have been Navidrome. Hopefully the make.conf settings have shut it all up.

You should see navidrome in the list. And realtek-re-kmod too. Cool.

At this point we can stop and exit the make.sh

We need to get the realtek module in place.

Adding the realtek-re-kmod

We should have built the driver now. We can install it into the image we are creating.

Check the path below is correct, the if_re.ko file was in a folder rtl_bsd_drv-ea4ed1e whcih apparently is the git hash, so the folder might be different.

install -v -o root -g wheel -m 555 \
    /usr/local/xigmanas/svn/build/ports/realtek-re-kmod/work/*/if_re.ko \
    /usr/local/xigmanas/rootfs/boot/modules

And now - back to /usr/local/xigmanas/svn/build/make.sh.

Select 2 and then 7 to continue below.

2.7 - Build Bootloader.

Yes - run this.

2.8 - Add Necessary Libraries.

Just run the first option - "Add required libraries". Becuase they are required. Duh.

2.9 - Modify File Permissions.

Just run it.

Carry on building

I create the following images, for testing and the real installation:

12) - Create 'LiveUSB.img.gz GPT' File.   (Rawrite to USB Key)
13) - Create 'LiveCD' (ISO) File.

Oh, we done!

Write the image

OK... how do I get it off the VM?

Earlier we made this directory in the home (root) folder on the VM ~/xigma

Mount this via sshfs.

sshfs -o port=2222 root@192.168.122.1:/usr/local/xigmanas ~/xigma

We should find

  • XigmaNAS-x64-LiveCD-14.3.0.5.10655.iso
  • XigmaNAS-x64-LiveUSB-GPT-14.3.0.5.10655.img.gz

We can mount the LiveCD ISO on another QEMU VM and test.

qemu-img create -f qcow2 xigmatest.qcow2 40G

# start with live cd
qemu-system-x86_64 -cpu host -enable-kvm -m 8192 -smp 4 \
  -cdrom ./XigmaNAS-x64-LiveCD-14.3.0.5.10655.iso \
  -drive file=./xigmatest.qcow2,format=qcow2 \
  -net nic -net user,hostfwd=tcp::2224-:22,hostfwd=tcp::8080-:80

# after installing, eject the cd, expose navidrome port 
qemu-system-x86_64 -cpu host -enable-kvm -m 8192 -smp 4 \
  -drive file=./xigmatest.qcow2,format=qcow2 \
  -net nic -net user,hostfwd=tcp::2224-:22,hostfwd=tcp::8080-:80,hostfwd=tcp::4533-:4533

You can install Xigmanas to this VM, configure the NIC's and DHCP. After install, shutdown the VM and restart without the CD.

You should get an IP like 10.0.2.15. I can access the web gui via http://localhost:8080, enable ssh. And all good.

Test realtek-re-kmod as best we can

Does the module exist?

ls -l /boot/modules/if_re.ko

Can we load the module - should get no errors.

kldload /boot/modules/if_re.ko

This VM does not have the hardware, so the rest of the config can happen later.

Test Navidrome

Copy the sample config:

cp /usr/local/etc/navidrome/config.toml.sample /usr/local/etc/navidrome/config.toml
service navidrome onestart

And hit it on http://localhost:4533.

Great. More config is needed, but that can happen on the real thing. Or practice here.

Install Xigmanas on your NAS

Backup your config.

Install xigmanas.

Restore config.

Configure realtek-re-kmod driver to load.

Log in to the default on the working nic so we can set up the boot loader.

Via the web gui:

Navigate to System>Advanced>loader.conf

Add two entries:

if_re_load="YES"
if_re_name="/boot/modules/if_re.ko"

These end up in the config.xml file as:

<loaderconf>
	...
	<param>
		<uuid>deadbeef-dead-c0de-face-8badcafef00d</uuid>
		<enable type="bool">1</enable>
		<name>if_re_load</name>
		<value>YES</value>
		<comment/>
	</param>
	<param>
		<uuid>deadbeef-dead-c0de-face-8badcafef00d</uuid>
		<enable type="bool">1</enable>
		<name>if_re_name</name>
		<value>/boot/modules/if_re.ko</value>
		<comment/>
	</param>

Navigate to System>Advanced>Command Scripts

In theory we should not need to do the following. In practice we do. I do not know why.

Add new preinit script with the command kldload if_re

Reboot.

Should now be able to configure the NIC to the realtek one.

Configure Navidrome

Read the navidrome freebsd config setup guide.

We need somewhere to store Navidrome's metadata. I made a new partition on my boot drive, but it could just be a folder on some disk.

I made /mnt/navidrome-data and mounted via the web gui so it is persistant.

We need a bunch of rc.conf. Navidrome will respect these settings over the config.toml.

	<name>navidrome_enable</name>
	<value>YES</value>

	<name>navidrome_datafolder</name>
	<value>/mnt/navidrome-data</value>

	<name>navidrome_config</name>
	<value>/mnt/navidrome-data/config.toml</value>

Edit the config.toml

Comment the ipaddress out so it responds on all nics and uncomment the port.

Via ssh to Xigmanas set:

chown -R www:www /mnt/navidrome-data

And reboot.

We can now hit the navidrome gui at http://192.168.1.xxx:4533

entry.title: Recover password on a vm
entry.content:
Recover password on a VM. Or any machine you have physical access to.

Oh I forgot my password. Not sure what happened really, copied the VM and now I cannot login.

Beware if you have EFS or encrypted files. You will probably have a bad time.

Create a WinPE ISO

Install the ADK, run Deployment tool as admin then run

 copype amd64 C:\WinPE_amd64
 MakeWinPEMedia /ISO C:\WinPE_amd64 C:\WinPE_amd64\WinPE_amd64.iso

Mount that ISO as a CD/DVD

Something something VM settings.

Force the VM to boot from CD

Edit the .vmx of your VM and add

 bios.forceSetupOnce = "TRUE"

Now the fun. I found my VM drive, D:

Hijack a system utility

D:
cd D:\windows\system32
ren utilman.exe utilman.exe.old
copy cmd.exe utilman.exe

Reboot.

At the password prompt open the accessibilty tools, that little icon at the bottom.

 whoami

I am system. That's handy.

Update password

 net user Administrator Password123

And login.

Voila.

entry.title: Less Worse Webforms
entry.content:
Routing

I seem to be unable to escape the horrific pit of despair that is ASP.NET WebForms, it's really starting to look like the Classic ASP of the um... noughties? Millennial something something? At any rate, there have at least been a couple of nice(r) features introduced to ease our suffering.

Routing is one of these, but to get the best out of it you'll also want to nuget in some Friendly Urls:

Install-Package Microsoft.AspNet.FriendlyUrls

A vanilla asp.net web application (in VS2013 at least) is kind enough to include this by default.

The Friendly Urls package includes a few things, and supports .NET 4, but for my purposes I care only for EnableFriendlyUrls() which will effectively turn on extensionless urls for a webforms project. Probably in your RouteConfig class:

    var settings = new FriendlyUrlSettings();
    routes.EnableFriendlyUrls(settings);

Armed with this and System.Web.Routing we can start to do less sucky things.

From .NET 4 System.Web.Routing is in the System.Web assembly, and so should be available to most new Web Forms applications. The MapPageRoute method lets us start to do nice(r) things.

For instance, we can map request values (query string or form) to placeholders in the url:

    routes.MapPageRoute("AboutRoute", "About/{param1}/{*param2}", "~/about.aspx");

And we can map arbitrary friendly urls to existing pages:

    routes.MapPageRoute("AnotherRoute", "TotallyFriendlyUrl/{param1}/{*param2}", "~/about.aspx");

In the second case there is no underlying page at TotallyFriendlyUrl.aspx so if the route is not matched correctly, i.e. /TotallyFriendlyUrl/this_bit_is_mandatory/this_bit_is_optional then a 404 will result.

Calls to /About/ will succeed for pretty much any parameters as 1) there is a page at about.aspx and 2) the param2 is a catch all.

Other bits

Quick, my beer is getting warm, we have an expression builder so we can make friendly urls declaratively in an aspx page:

<asp:HyperLink ID="HyperLink5" runat="server" 
    NavigateUrl="<%$RouteUrl:locale=CA,year=2009,routename=salesroute%>">
    Sales Report - CA, 2009
</asp:HyperLink>

And [FriendlyUrlSegments] parameter attribute for um.. doing things like model binding to a method and junk. And also [Form] and [QueryString] to boot.

The friendly url package also allows to do something that MVC 4 (or was it from an earlier version?) can do out of the box, namely chuck a device specific view in, e.g.

  • about.aspx
  • about.mobile.aspx

Unfortunately this does not seem to play well with the other children. So adding an about.mobile.aspx you might expect the uh... attractive /totallyfriendlyurl/oh/hai/ route to dish up a mobile specific view. It did not. Given we stated that the route mapped to about.aspx it's not that surprising, but it would have been nice if it was magic and just worked.

To be fair I'm not sure where I can be using this stuff. WebForms work is either some legacy hell that would break as soon as you started doing this (and mobile support? Ha!) or is piggy backing on top of Umbraco or SiteCore which takes care of (some) of this stuff for you anyway. No-one in their right mind would start a green fields webforms project today? Right? Amiright?

entry.title: Web Transforms for external files
entry.content:
So often it's easy to come up with the complex solution and hard to do the simplest thing. And sometimes it's a case of just not seeing the wood for the trees.

When working with systems like Sitecore or Umbraco you find a lot of external config files. Sitecore has it's patching (a kind of custom transform engine) and there's always web transforms, but what to do about environmental differences in all those external files?

The complex way

All we wanted was to be able to "add transform" to any old config file. So we reach for solutions like SlowCheetah or msbuild scripts using Web Transform Task and others.

It works and seems easy enough (expecially SlowCheetah).

But now any one coming to the project has friction and has to install a Visual Studio extension, or god forbid, edit an msbuild script.

The simple way

Rather than trying to transform the external config file, we just need to transform the path to the file.

Like a light bulb. So simple. So obvious. Took so long to recognise it.

Just a bunch of config files with each environment in the name.

Add a web transform and use the Condition locator. Say Web.Staging.config:

    <myModule configsource="config/myModule.<strong>STAGING</strong>.config" 
          xdt:Locator="Condition(@configSource='config/myModule.config')" 
          xdt:Transfrom="Replace" />

Sure, you don't get nicely nested files in the solution explorer, and it's not completely DRY. But it's simple. And easy. And it works.

But

You will end up deploying multiple config files, e.g. myModule.config, mymodule.staging.config etc. and that might be an issue if there are sensitive settings in there, like connection strings or passwords.

Cheers.

entry.title: Simulating Content PlaceHolder without MasterPages
entry.content:
Oh back in the deeply wrong world of WebForms...

So somewhere in the misty depths of an ASPX page I wish to render out all the scraps of javascript that any ASCX user controls may require. You could use the ScriptManager and RegisterClientScriptBlock (and LoadScriptsBeforeUI=false), or be very tidy and bundle and minify all the little script snippets together.

Other times it is desirable to just keep all the HTML and script together in a single ASCX.

With a master page we can use ContentPlaceHolder, but in just a normal ASPX page?

Behold. Add a placeholder to the ASPX, prehaps at the bottom of the page.

<asp:PlaceHolder runat="server" ID="ScriptsPlaceHolder"></asp:PlaceHolder>

In the user control we have a little javascript snippet, prehaps to hook up a click event. Who knows.

    html normally goes here

    <my:RenderPlaceHolder runat="server" PlaceHolderId="ScriptsPlaceHolder">
        <content>
           <script type="text/javascript">
              console.log('this script is rendered from a user control 
								into it's parents placeholder');
           </script>        
        </content>
    </my:RenderPlaceHolder>

The RenderPlaceHolder control will look up into the page and find the corresponding PlaceHolder control, dumping it's content into it.

    using System.Web.UI;

    [ParseChildren(true, "Content")]
    [PersistChildren(false)]
    public class RenderPlaceHolder : UserControl
    {
        protected override void Render(HtmlTextWriter writer)
        {
            // you should probably do some null reference checks here...
            Page.FindControl(PlaceHolderId).Controls.Add(Content);
            base.Render(writer);
        }

        public Control Content { get; set; }

        public string PlaceHolderId { get; set; }
    }

entry.title: Resolving strategies by key
entry.content:
I have been abusing the strategy pattern of late, and ended up writing a StrategyResolver class.

This sort of thing is probably best left to a DI container, using a factory to resolve. But anyways...

We can inject a StrategyResolver<TStrategy> for our strategy implementations, and then Resolve the correct strategy based on a key.

This lets use resolve the strategy through data. For example, I've been doing a bit web scraping and manipulation, so using this technique I can resolve a strategy based on the domain of the page I am processing.

I guess I'm really just injecting a factory. Sort of.

	// create a resolver (or inject one)
    StrategyResolver _strategyResolver = new StrategyResolver<IMyStrategyInterface>();
	
    // use it to retrieve an implementation based on some key
    _myStrategy = _strategyResolver.Resolve(url.Host);

	// create and decorate your strategy implementation
    [StrategyFor("news.ycombinator.com")]
    public class HackerNewsStrategy : IMyStrategyInterface

The resolver scans the calling assembly for implementations of TStrategy. When any are found they are stashed away in a dictionary.

Later we can retrieve them by the key. If nothing is found then we will return the default(TStrategy), which is probably going to be null.

Whether this is a good implementation or idea or not, I am finding it quite nice to be able to just add a new class implementing my IStrategy, decorate it and... that's it. Done.

The resolver class:

    public class StrategyResolver<TStrategy> 
    {
        private static Dictionary<string, TStrategy> _strategies;

        public TStrategy Resolve(string key)
        {
            var assembly = Assembly.GetCallingAssembly();

            return ResolveImpl(key, assembly);
        }

        public TStrategy Resolve(string key, TStrategy defaultStrategy)
        {
            var assembly = Assembly.GetCallingAssembly();

            return ResolveImpl(key, assembly, defaultStrategy);
        }

        private static TStrategy ResolveImpl(string key, Assembly callingAssembly, TStrategy defaultStrategy = default(TStrategy))
        {
            if (_strategies == null) Load(callingAssembly);

            var lowerKey = key.ToLowerInvariant();

            if (_strategies != null && _strategies.ContainsKey(lowerKey))
            {
                return _strategies[lowerKey];
            }

            return defaultStrategy;
        }

        private static void Load(Assembly assembly)
        {
            _strategies = new Dictionary<string, TStrategy>();

            var strategyType = typeof(TStrategy);
            var types = assembly
                .GetTypes()
                .Where(t => strategyType.IsAssignableFrom(t) && t.IsClass)
                .ToList();

            foreach (var type in types)
            {
                var strategyFor = type.GetCustomAttributes(typeof(StrategyForAttribute), false).FirstOrDefault();

                if (strategyFor == null) continue;

                var strategyForAttribute = strategyFor as StrategyForAttribute;

                if (strategyForAttribute == null) continue;

                _strategies[strategyForAttribute.Key] = (TStrategy)Activator.CreateInstance(type);
            }
        }
    }

Each strategy implementation is decorated with the [StrategyFor] attribute.

    [AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Class)]
    public class StrategyForAttribute : Attribute
    {
        public StrategyForAttribute(string key)
        {
            Key = key;
        }

        public string Key { get; private set; }
    }

entry.title: Synchronize dispatcher and caller
entry.content:
More Windows Phone/Silverlight/WPF/(and probably WinRT) goodness.

Sometimes you want to know that any work pushed to the UI dispatcher has completed. For awhile I worked with the idea that Thread.Sleep(1) would let any pending work complete. It doesn't.

A much better approach is to use some thread signalling. The calling thread will wait until the dispatched work has completed, or give up after some period.


        private static void WaitWithDispatcher(Action action)
        {
            if (Deployment.Current.Dispatcher.CheckAccess())
            {
                action();
                return;
            }

            var wait = new AutoResetEvent(false);

            Deployment.Current.Dispatcher.BeginInvoke(() =>
            {
                try
                {
                    action();
                }
                finally
                {
                    // always signal so code can continue
                    wait.Set();
                }
            });

            // wait for a reasonable period for dispatcher to complete
            wait.WaitOne(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10));
        }

        private static void WithDispatcher(Action action)
        {
            if (Deployment.Current.Dispatcher.CheckAccess())
            {
                action();
                return;
            }

            Deployment.Current.Dispatcher.BeginInvoke(action);
        }

entry.title: Better CSV downloads
entry.content:
To often when offering a simple "save as CSV" function I see code that simply makes the database request, strings it up and sends it down the wire.

And more than once I have written code like this.

It's generally not a problem if:

  • the requested data is small
  • you have very few users
  • you do not care about the impact on your servers memory

We can do better, and in a fairly simple way.

By using an IQueryable<T> and paging we can easily limit the memory usage by only streaming one page at a time back to the user.

This does have the downside of making multiple database requests, but I believe that to be preferable to simply pulling all the data at once.

Here we simply skip and take over the query. My ToCsv code is a bit ropey and only does what I need, but there are plenty of similar functions to be found around the interwebs.

Whenever you make a database request, be it for downloading results or just populating a grid, you should always considering limiting the results. There are very few times when the user really wants 100,000 records at once.

Usage:


    using (var context = new DataContext())
            {
                var code = Request.QueryString["code"];

                // query and project to a flat structure for CSV
                var earnings = context.StockEarnings.Where(
                    s => s.StockCode == code)
                    .Select(earning => new
                    {
                        earning.StockCode,
                        earning.Year,
                        earning.Margin,
                        earning.CashFlow,
                        earning.ROE
                    }).AsQueryable();  // note that AsQueryable

                DownloadHelper.DownloadAsCsv(Context, earnings, code + "_earnings.csv");
            }



    public static void DownloadAsCsv<T>(HttpContext httpContext, IQueryable<T> query, string fileName, int pageSize = 500) where T : class
        {
            var pageNumber = 0;

            while (true)
            {
                var results = query.Skip(pageSize * pageNumber).Take(pageSize);

                if (!results.Any()) break;

                var csv = results.ToCsv();

                if (pageNumber == 0)
                {
                    var properties = typeof(T).GetProperties();
                    // a bit of reflection to generate the header row
                    var header = properties.Aggregate("", (current, propertyInfo) => current + string.Format("{0},", propertyInfo.Name));

                    header = header.TrimEnd(',');
                    header += "\r\n";

                    csv = csv.Insert(0, header);

                    httpContext.Response.Clear();
                    httpContext.Response.AddHeader("Content-Disposition",
                                                   "attachment; filename='" + fileName + "'");
                    httpContext.Response.ContentType = "text/comma-separated-values";
                }

                pageNumber++;

                httpContext.Response.Write(csv);
                // flush starts sending the response back to the user
                httpContext.Response.Flush();
            }

            httpContext.Response.End();
        }

    public static string ToCsv<T>(this IEnumerable<T> items)
            where T : class
        {
            var csvBuilder = new StringBuilder();
            var properties = typeof(T).GetProperties();

            foreach (T item in items)
            {
                var line = string.Join(",", properties.Select(p => p.GetValue(item, null).ToCsvValue()).ToArray());
                csvBuilder.AppendLine(line);
            }

            return csvBuilder.ToString();
        }

        private static string ToCsvValue<T>(this T item)
        {
            if (item == null) return "\"\"";

            if (item is string)
            {
                return string.Format("\"{0}\"", item.ToString().Replace("\"", "\\\""));
            }

            double dummy;

            if (double.TryParse(item.ToString(), out dummy))
            {
                return string.Format("{0}", item);
            }

            return string.Format("\"{0}\"", item);
        }

entry.title: Detect wifi on Windows Phone
entry.content:
If you are making web requests on the windows phone you should check network availability first.

     Microsoft.Phone.Net.NetworkInformation.DeviceNetworkInformation.IsNetworkAvailable

If you are trying to be a conscientious developer you may only want to make web requests when the phone is connected to a wifi network, for instance in a background agent update.

The API offers:

     DeviceNetworkInformation.IsWiFiEnabled

This, however only tells you the user has wifi enabled. It does not tell you if the phone is connected and using a wifi network.

You must also check the NetworkInterfaceType. Note that the majority of interface types are not supported on the phone. There is really only Wireless80211, MobileBroadbandGsm and MobileBroadbandCdma to worry about. I believe Ethernet is available when connected to a PC with Zune running, as I think Zune allows the phone to piggy back off the PC's network connection. AFAIK.

    NetworkInterface.NetworkInterfaceType == NetworkInterfaceType.Wireless80211

Put it all together.


        private bool IsWifiConnected()
        {
            if(IsNetworkAvailable() && IsWifiEnabled())
            {
                return NetworkInterface.NetworkInterfaceType == NetworkInterfaceType.Wireless80211;
            }

            return false;
        }

        private bool IsWifiEnabled()
        {
            return DeviceNetworkInformation.IsWiFiEnabled;
        }

        private bool IsNetworkAvailable()
        {
            return DeviceNetworkInformation.IsNetworkAvailable;
        }

This thing is slooooow

After implementing something like this in a background agent on the phone, I was surprised to see the agent frequently not running correctly, usually timing out.

As far as as I can tell, the call to NetworkInterface.NetworkInterfaceType can be very slow, sometimes 20-30 seconds, and sometimes simply returning None, even though the phone is clearly connected to the network.

People on stackoverflow suggest wrapping these calls up in some async pattern, either threadpool or whatever, as it will be a blocking call otherwise.

In the case of a background agent I can't see how to determine if we are on a wifi network (or connected at all) in a timely manner. The background task must complete in, I think, 25 seconds or so. If the network takes 20-30 seconds, well you can see the problem.

WIFI is sleeping

The phone has certain behaviors you must be aware of.

  • wifi will turn off if the phone is asleep
  • the phone will preferentially use the mobile connection

On the windows phone 8 a recent update allows the user to specify "Keep WiFi on when screen times out".

On windows phone 7.5 it seems to keep WiFi on by default. I am not sure.

Basically, during a background task:

  • if the user has wifi enabled and mobile data turned on the phone will opt for mobile data
  • if the user has wifi enabled and wifi enabled during sleep (and mobile data) the phone should opt for wifi
  • if the user has wifi enabled, wifi enabled during sleep and mobile data off, the check for network will succeed (uses wifi)
  • if the user has wifi enabled, mobile data off, the check for network will fail (timeout)
  • if the user has wifi disabled, mobile data on, the check for network will succeed (uses mobile data)

At the end of the day the best you can do is inform your users.

"If you wish to use wifi for background data requests please check "Keep WiFi on when screen times out" is enabled under the advanced settings of your wifi connection."
